instructions: Peel the bottle gourd and grate it on the large holes of a box grater. That should be about 3 cups.
Transfer the grated gourd to a bowl, toss it with 1/2 tsp of the salt, and let it sit for 5 minutes. Squeeze it hard in a clean towel over a measuring cup. Keep the liquid for the gravy.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion. Mince the garlic and grate the ginger together. Roughly chop the tomatoes.

Put the squeezed gourd back in the bowl. Add 1/3 cup of the gram flour, 1/2 tsp of the turmeric, 1/2 tsp of the chili powder and the garam masala. Mix well. If it feels wet, add the rest of the gram flour a spoonful at a time. It should hold a ball when you press it.
Shape the mixture into 12 balls, a little smaller than a golf ball. Roll them in the cornstarch to coat.

Heat 1 cup of the oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat until a pinch of the mixture sizzles right away. Fry the koftas in 2 batches for 3 to 4 minutes each, turning them, until they're golden brown. Transfer them to a paper towel-lined plate.
While the second batch fries, heat 2 tsp of the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes and cashews with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes break down. Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for a few minutes. Blend until smooth, with no added water.

Heat the remaining 2 tsp oil in the same pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and bay leaf and let them sizzle for 15 seconds. Stir in the remaining 1/2 tsp turmeric and the remaining 1 tsp chili powder.
Pour in the blended paste and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the oil separates at the edges. Stir in the coriander powder and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Add the squeezed gourd liquid and enough water to make 1 1/2 cups. Bring it to a boil, then simmer for 3 minutes.
Off the heat, crush the kasuri methi between your palms and stir it in. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Arrange the koftas in a serving bowl, pour the gravy over them, and scatter the cilantro on top. Serve with roti or rice.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead, 4.99 from 254 ratings) grates and squeezes bottle gourd, binds it with gram flour, fries the koftas, and serves them in an onion, tomato and cashew gravy with the squeezed gourd water added back. Other pages (Spice Up the Curry, Whisk Affair) bake, steam or air fry the koftas, or use a yogurt-based gravy. The curd in Hebbar's gravy is left out so it stays vegan and dairy-free; the gourd liquid and water make up the sauce. Scaled up so the koftas feed four, and it runs close to 50 minutes with the frying.
